_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 32 (Mahanaim; Esau gifts; Peniel wrestling). Saadia-specific: v.2 'מלאיכה' אללה' = 'angels of God' (intermediation, not God Himself encountering Jacob); v.3 'ד'את אלעסכרין' = 'the place of the two camps' for מחנים; v.4 'בלד אדום' = 'land of Edom' (Saadia identifies שעיר=אלשראה as Edom); v.25 'שכ'צא' = 'a figure' (Saadia keeps it ambiguous — not explicitly 'man' or 'angel'); v.29 'תרווסת ענד אללה ועד אלנאס' = 'you have been chief before God and before people' (Saadia's gloss for שרית — the etymology of Israel as 'chief/ruler').

translations.1: And Laban rose early in the morning, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them; then he departed, and returned to his place.
translations.2: And Jacob went on his way; and the angels of God met him.
translations.3: And when Jacob saw them, he said: 'This is God's army.' And he named that place The Place of the Two Camps (Mahanaim).
translations.4: Then Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, to the land of al-Sharah, to the land of Edom.
translations.5: And he charged them, saying: 'Thus shall you say: "To my lord Esau — thus said your servant Jacob: I have dwelt with Laban, and lingered until now.
translations.6: And I have come to have cattle and donkeys, and sheep and male and female slaves; and I have sent to tell my lord — that I might find favor with you."'
translations.7: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying: 'We came to your brother, to Esau — and behold, he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men with him.'
translations.8: And Jacob was greatly afraid, and the matter pressed upon him. And he divided the people who were with him, and the sheep, and the cattle, and the camels, into two camps.
translations.9: And he said: 'If Esau comes to one of them and strikes it, the remaining camp shall be spared.'
translations.10: Then Jacob said: 'O God of my grandfather Abraham, and God of my father Isaac — O God who said to me, "Return to your land and your birthplace, and I shall do good to you" —
translations.11: I am less than worthy of the kindness and the goodness which You have done with Your servant — for with my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
translations.12: I ask You to deliver me from the hand of my brother — from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and slay me, mothers along with sons — cruelty!
translations.13: And You have said: I shall do good to you, and I shall make your offspring as the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted from its abundance.'
translations.14: And he lodged there that night; and he set apart from what he had brought — a gift for Esau his brother:
translations.15: two hundred she-goats and twenty he-goats; two hundred ewes and twenty rams;
translations.16: thirty nursing camels with their young; forty cows and ten bulls; twenty she-asses and ten foals.
translations.17: And he gave them to his servants — each drove apart by itself. And he said to them: 'Pass on before me, and set a space between drove and drove.'
translations.18: And he commanded the first, saying: 'When Esau my brother meets you, and asks you, saying, "Whose are you, and where are you going, and to whom belong these before you?"
translations.19: you shall say: "To your servant Jacob; this is a gift sent to my lord Esau — and behold, he too is behind us."'
translations.20: And he commanded the second likewise, and the third, and the rest of those going on with the droves, saying: 'Thus shall you say to Esau, when you meet him —
translations.21: and say also: "And behold, your servant Jacob is behind us."' For he said: 'I shall appease him first with the gift going on before me; and after that I shall look upon his face — perhaps he shall accept me.'
translations.22: And the gift went on before him; but he himself lodged that night in the camp.
translations.23: And he arose that night, and took his two wives and his two maidservants and his eleven sons; and he crossed over the ford of Yabbok with them.
translations.24: And he took them, and brought them across the wadi; and he brought across all that he had.
translations.25: And Jacob was left alone. And a figure wrestled with him until the dawn rose.
translations.26: And when he saw that he could not prevail against him, he touched the socket of his thigh; and the socket of Jacob's thigh was dislocated in his wrestling with him.
translations.27: And when the dawn rose, he said: 'Let me go, for the dawn has risen.' He said: 'I shall not let you go unless you bless me.'
translations.28: He said to him: 'What is your name?' He said: 'Jacob.'
translations.29: He said: 'Your name shall not be called Jacob alone any more, but Israel — for you have been chief before God and before people, and have prevailed.'
translations.30: And Jacob asked him, and said: 'Tell me, what is your name?' He said: 'Why do you ask my name?' And he blessed him there.
translations.31: And Jacob named that place Peniel, saying: 'I have seen the angel of God face to face, and my soul has been delivered.'
translations.32: And the sun rose for him, as he passed Penuel; and he was limping on his thigh until that time.
translations.33: Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sciatic nerve which is upon the socket of the thigh, to this day — because he touched the socket of Jacob's thigh, at the sciatic nerve.
